title: Implicit High-Order Moment Tensor Estimation and Learning Latent Variable Models
authors: Ilias Diakonikolas (University of Wisconsin-Madison, USA), Daniel M. Kane (University of California, San Diego, USA)
abstract: We study the general task of of learning latent-variable models in high dimensions with many hidden parameters. A common technique to address this task algorithmically is (some version of) the method of moments. Unfortunately, moment-based approaches are often hampered by the fact that the moment tensors of super-constant degree cannot even be written down in polynomial time. Motivated by such learning applications, we develop a general efficient algorithm for implicit moment tensor computation. Roughly speaking, our algorithm computes in polynomial time a succinct approximate description of certain higher order tensors assuming that there exists an unbiased estimator for each tensor with small variance that takes an appropriately nice form. Our framework broadly generalizes, both conceptually and technically, prior work which developed an efficient algorithm for the specific moment tensors that arise in the task of clustering mixtures of spherical Gaussians. By leveraging our implicit moment estimation algorithm, we obtain the first polynomial-time learning algorithms for several classical latent-variable models-thereby resolving or making significant progress towards a number of important open problems in the literature. These include learning mixtures of linear regressions, learning mixtures of spherical Gaussians, and learning positive linear combinations of non-linear activations.
